FN-6YBJ731-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 233
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Representative Ed Oliver
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 02/24/2026
House Bill 233 as introduced would increase the obligations of the Alabama National Guard
Education Assistance Program (ANGEAP) by an undetermined amount dependent on any
tuition assistance provided for: (1) accredited and non-accredited but approved certification or
stand-alone training as part of a workforce development program; and (2) required on-campus
living expenses or meal plans.
Additionally, this bill would decrease potential obligations of the ANGEAP by an undetermined
amount dependent on the difference in: (1) payments for tuition, fees, ancillary costs, and costs
of required on-campus living expenses and meal plans at an amount not to exceed the median
cost of tuition per term of all public four-year institutions of higher education in the state; and
(2) payments made under current law. For the 2025-26 school year the median cost of tuition per
term is $12,454.
The Governor's recommended Education Trust Fund budget for FY 2027 would appropriate
$9,831,114 to the ANGEAP.

FN-6YBJ731-2
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 233
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Representative Ed Oliver
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 03/03/2026
House Bill 233 as reported by the Committee on Ways and Means Education would increase
the obligations of the Alabama National Guard Education Assistance Program (ANGEAP) by an
undetermined amount dependent on any tuition assistance provided for: (1) accredited and
non-accredited but approved certification or stand-alone training as part of a workforce
development program; and (2) required on-campus living expenses or meal plans.
Additionally, this bill would decrease potential obligations of the ANGEAP by an undetermined
amount dependent on the difference in: (1) payments for tuition, fees, ancillary costs, and costs
of required on-campus living expenses and meal plans at an amount not to exceed the median
cost of tuition per term of all public four-year institutions of higher education in the state; and
(2) payments made under current law. For the 2025-26 school year the median cost of tuition per
term is $12,454.
This bill would also provide for funds to remain in the fund at the end of the fiscal year and not
revert to the funding source, except for appropriated funds.
The Governor's recommended Education Trust Fund budget for FY 2027 would appropriate
$9,831,114 to the ANGEAP.
